easy.def: To straighten out something that was wrapped, or to relax.
examples: Unwind the string.
I unwind after school.
She unwound the yarn.

more.def: To undo something that was wound up or wrapped, or to relax after work.
examples: I unwound the string from the kite.
Dad likes to unwind by reading a book after work.
She unwound the scarf from her neck.
It is unwise to run on ice.
That was an unwise choice.
He made an unwise move.

more.def: Not sensible, or likely to cause trouble.
examples: It is unwise to run on a wet floor.
He made an unwise choice and forgot his coat.
It would be unwise to swim in a storm.

easy.def: Not good enough or not deserving.
examples: He felt unworthy.
An unworthy prize.
An unworthy act.

more.def: Not good enough, or not deserving of something.
examples: He felt unworthy of the prize because his friend had helped him.
An unworthy act brings shame.
The lazy knight was unworthy of the king's trust.

easy.def: To take off the paper around something.
examples: I unwrap the gift.
She unwrapped the present.
He will unwrap it.

more.def: To take off the paper or cover that is wrapped around something.
examples: I unwrapped the gift with a big smile.
She unwrapped a sandwich.
He unwrapped the candy.
It is an unwritten rule.
The unwritten story.
An unwritten law.

more.def: Not written down but still understood or followed.
examples: It is an unwritten rule to say thank you.
The story is unwritten and told by mouth.
There is an unwritten rule to be quiet in the library.
Unzip your coat.
I unzipped my bag.
She will unzip the tent.

more.def: To open something that closes with a zipper.
examples: He unzipped his jacket because it was warm.
She unzipped the tent and crawled out.
Please unzip the backpack and get your lunch.
